venture.headline: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
venture.summary: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.

venture.headline: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
venture.summary: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.

research.headline: Tiny Gradient Edits Fix Small Language Model Thinking Loops
research.summary: Fine-tuning a small language model on its own correct answers using gradients fixes thinking loops and raises MATH-500 accuracy to 39.0-45.5%. Combining this gradient edit with a frontier model weight edit reaches a score of 62.2% at 32k tokens. The gradient concentrates on the most nearly constant channels of the first three layers, acting as a constant vector added to the residual stream.

research.headline: Distilling long-horizon policies from teacher actions enables cross-format transfer without hidden chains-of-thought
research.summary: Researchers demonstrate that long-horizon policies can be distilled from teacher actions alone without needing the teacher's hidden chain-of-thought, using a KL loss to limit drift. The resulting student models exhibit cross-format transfer, carrying over performance to inference with thinking enabled and improving task success rates across benchmarks. Introducing short summaries called CoT-proxies further boosts student performance when distilling from both open and closed teachers.

research.headline: OmniAct cross-embodiment manipulation policy achieves high success across diverse robots
research.summary: OmniAct is a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that conditions directly on robot kinematics and scene context to produce embodiment-specific behavior. Trained on one million procedurally designed simulated embodiments, the policy achieves a 63.0% success rate on evaluation episodes and outperforms baseline methods on unseen real-world robots.

research.headline: SAG-Mem Framework Enhances Long-Term Conversational Memory via Lexical Expansion
research.summary: SAG-Mem preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and uses query-time lexical expansion to discover complementary evidence without requiring model inference for memory construction. The framework achieves the highest overall scores on the LoCoMo and LongMemEval benchmarks among evaluated methods, while the SAG-Mem-Lite configuration achieves lower operational costs and low query latency.

research.summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. titans.summary: Amazon has held talks about letting Meta's Muse AI agent shop on its online marketplace, according to a report from Fortune. The discussions, which could end Amazon's block on Muse, reportedly center on the kinds of products the AI agent recommends and the potential impact on the ecommerce giant's advertising revenue. regulatory.headline: SHEIN Will Pay $100 Million to Settle FTC Deceptive Practice Allegations
regulatory.summary: SHEIN will pay $100 million in consumer redress to settle Federal Trade Commission allegations of unfair and deceptive practices. The FTC alleged that the fast-fashion retailer suppressed negative reviews, failed to keep shipping promises, and made deceptive claims regarding its supply chain and cotton origin. Furthermore, the agency stated SHEIN made it unreasonably difficult for consumers to resolve purchase issues.

regulatory.headline: Ten Additional States Join FTC Lawsuit Against Dollar General
regulatory.summary: Ten states joined the FTC's amended complaint as co-plaintiffs in a lawsuit against Dollar General Corporation. The lawsuit alleges the company engaged in deceptive pricing practices by charging customers more at the register than the advertised shelf prices, resulting in millions of dollars in consumer costs.

regulatory.headline: FTC Finalizes Antitrust Order Governing Beretta and Ruger Deal
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission has finalized an order addressing antitrust concerns from a stock purchase agreement between Beretta Holding S.A. and Sturm, Ruger & Co. Inc. The measure resolves regulatory issues by barring anticompetitive entanglements between the two major firearm manufacturers.

macro.headline: Inflation gets worse. Now the Fed no choice but to raise U.S. interest rates.
macro.summary: The measure of inflation used by the Federal Reserve to influence U.S. interest rates rose again in October at an accelerated rate, virtually assuring the central bank will increase borrowing costs next month.

macro.headline: Nvidia’s stock is giving back more than half of Monday’s rally as dip buyers cash in
macro.summary: Based on where retail investors bought Nvidia’s stock on the dip last week, their gains are nearly all gone, according to Vanda Research.

frontier.headline: Physicists trap and cool a positron near absolute zero
frontier.summary: Physicists successfully suspended and cooled a positron in a wall-free trap to separate it safely from ordinary matter. The team plans to conduct the most precise comparison yet between matter and antimatter. Any discovered differences could expose cracks in the Standard Model of particle physics.

frontier.headline: Ultrathin titanium seed layer enables robust room-temperature growth of alpha-tantalum on sapphire
frontier.summary: Researchers demonstrate a reliable room-temperature method for growing alpha-phase tantalum films on sapphire substrates using an ultrathin titanium seed layer. The resulting coplanar-waveguide resonators achieve two-level-system-limited quality factors comparable to current state-of-the-art standards. Additionally, temperature-dependent evaluations show that growth methods and post-processing treatments directly influence microwave performance by introducing temperature-activated losses.

frontier.headline: A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected
frontier.summary: ESA’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, despite being designed to study distant galaxies and the mysteries of the dark Universe. The icy object is approximately 1.3 billion kilometers from Earth and follows an unusual orbit that takes thousands of years to complete.

frontier.headline: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
frontier.summary: IBM and University of Chicago researchers have demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. A novel error-detection technique also allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.

frontier.headline: Evolutionary constraints on protein fold diversity
frontier.summary: Arrangements of secondary structures in proteins yield a wide variety of possible topologies, yet the protein folds observed in nature are limited in their diversity. Is the number of protein folds limited by biophysical constraints or by evolutionary contingency? In recent years, the development of new methods for protein structure prediction and comparison, molecular design, and the rapid progress of cryo-electron microscopy revealed new insights into the protein fold space.

industry.headline: Inside the Chinese City Where Furniture Dupes Are Made
industry.summary: Across social media, influencers share the fake luxury pieces they got directly from China—for one-tenth the price. Here’s where that viral sofa came from.

voices.headline: Conservatives Invoke Western Civilization Myth to Justify Political Power
voices.summary: Donald Trump and the MAGA movement have increasingly framed the U.S. as the defender of Western civilization to legitimize claims of superiority and dominance. Critics argue this narrative relies on an outdated, mythologized view of history that ignores the interconnected, cross-cultural exchanges actually driving human progress.

voices.headline: Donald Trump Pushes to Reinstate Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
voices.summary: Donald Trump intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO despite reports linking Huang to a Chinese spy agency and chip transfers to China. Trump defended the decision, claiming he discussed the matter with Chinese President Xi Jinping, while showing disregard for potential national security impacts.

voices.headline: The Misguided Democratic Opposition to Permitting Reform
voices.summary: In a break with Congress’s Orwellian naming conventions, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is genuinely bipartisan, pro-affordability, and would create some jobs. Although affordability is a popular concept—the entire Democratic Party campaigned on it in the midterm elections—it isn’t easy to execute. Bringing down inflation by reducing the budget deficit would require painful choices to raise taxes or cut spending.

voices.headline: The Great American Tradition
voices.summary: In September, after the White House barred CNN journalists from its grounds, some of the top news organizations in the country suspended their pooled coverage there. The Department of Justice is now investigating them for this act of defiance. In a statement, a department spokesperson accused the networks of having “proudly boycotted covering White House events” and warned that “group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act.” This argument is not a new one.
